nodes.name: Aksa
nodes.brief: Aksa is a wandering swordmaster and a drunk who cannot get drunk. He appears to be about fifty, he is missing his left arm at the shoulder, and to everyone who meets him he is a scarred veteran with a good sword-hand and a story nobody wants to ask about.

nodes.name: Alamna
nodes.brief: The current Wing of Freedom and member of The Winds of Freedom, Alamna is a common-blooded Faalari who's dedicated her life to exploration and descovery. ## Appearance and personality

nodes.name: Aldric Roquenegra
nodes.brief: Aldric Roquenegra is Lord of House Roquenegra and of La Marca, and he is thirty-nine. He holds the northern border against Kurogane and he has never been cut in combat. He co-leads the house with his wife Sela Roquenegra: he takes the soldiers and the fortresses, she takes the court.

nodes.name: Alénor
nodes.brief: Alénor is queen of Arvela, forty-five, and the last of house Vardanel — a lesser house, not the royal one. She married into the crown; the blood belongs to Argavel. She has co-governed the kingdom in substance for twenty years. She married Argavel for love, which scandalised the court at the time, and she has outlasted the scandal by the simple method of being better at politics than anyone who raised it.

nodes.name: Argavel
nodes.brief: Argavel is the reigning king of Arvela, forty-seven years old, a capable and just monarch who is dying publicly and by his own decision. Everyone at court knows he is ill. Nobody knows the illness matches no catalogue.

nodes.name: Baldric Roquenegra
nodes.brief: Baldric is the bishop who holds the Inquisition, and Aldric Roquenegra's younger brother. He deserted the front once, and everything he has built since has been built on top of it.

nodes.name: Bastyr
nodes.brief: Bastyr is the current leader of The Winged Protectors, on of The Four major clans of The Faalari. He is also the current Wing of Battle, one of the Wings of Choice and leader of the Skyborn. ## Appearance and personality

nodes.name: Bernal de Quilmar
nodes.brief: Elder brother of Mencía Santaella de Quilmar, disinherited, one-armed, and convinced that Lord Santaella murdered his sister.

nodes.name: Bras
nodes.brief: Bras is forty-one and leads the March Mages, the unlicensed unit that House Roquenegra hides in its border fortresses and uses as its de facto elite. He is a master of stealth and, quietly, one of the most technically accomplished living users of Solar magic.

nodes.name: Cira Santaella
nodes.brief: Cira Santaella is twenty-three and the heir of House Santaella. At court she is visible, controlled, devout, and strikingly beautiful. She performs the faith for a father who does not know her.

nodes.name: Corian de la Marca
nodes.brief: Corian de la Marca is twenty-three, a minor noble of La Marca with no title of any weight, and a frontier soldier. He is currently on a court stay in Altosangre and returns to the March seasonally.

nodes.name: Des Terrao
nodes.brief: A pure-blood Homura — the wrath lineage, the heavy red ones who hold the border and to whom the duel is both code and food — and a blood-magic practitioner who uses it on **himself** — driving his own body past what an oni body does. He was a respected fighter with a title to match it.

nodes.name: Don Enfadao
nodes.brief: The Homura Lord, holder of one of the two blood seats on the Council of Demon Lords, and a pure-blood of very great age — the elder of the two seats by a wide margin.

nodes.name: Eirvel
nodes.brief: Eirvel — the name is a pseudonym — is the sole master of La Vela and a pure-blood elf of very great age. He travels under cover as an itinerant copyist and has no fixed home.

nodes.name: Erasmo del Gal
nodes.brief: Erasmo del Gal is Royal Physician of Arvela, fifty-two, and has tended the royal family for eleven years. He is competent, trusted, and above suspicion.

nodes.name: Ilvaen
nodes.brief: Ilvaen is **The Strand** of the Court of Silk — the finest of the seven seats, and the most invisible. She holds the realm of the Nadir, inside their hollow mountain, and she has been there longer than any living Nadir remembers.

nodes.name: Ithanel
nodes.brief: Ithanel is a princess of Arvela, twin to Vareth and, like him, an undeclared co-claimant to the throne of their dying father Argavel. She is twenty-three. Where her brother is the soldier of the pair, she is the machinery: she reads the working parts of a government the way he reads terrain, and she is beloved in the lower quarter of Valdecorona in a way no one at court has thought to find significant.

nodes.name: Lartasez
nodes.brief: The current leader of The Winds of Freedom. A seasoned crafter and resented leader. He is known as one of the best crafters in The Faalari. ## Appearance and personality

nodes.name: Lord Santaella
nodes.brief: Lord Santaella is the head of House Santaella and he is sixty-three. His family uses the house name and not given names, which tells you most of what the house believes about itself.

nodes.name: Mencía Santaella de Quilmar
nodes.brief: The wife of Lord Santaella and mother of Cira Santaella. She died of an illness when Cira was small, after years in bed, and there is nothing strange about the death.

nodes.name: Miedo Miedin
nodes.brief: The Kurayami Lord, holder of the second blood seat on the Council of Demon Lords. Pure-blood, and **the younger of the two seats** — he came to it comparatively recently, where Don Enfadao has held his for centuries.

nodes.name: Miren
nodes.brief: Miren is personal maid to Princess Ithanel, twenty-six years old, and passes without difficulty for competent household staff of unremarkable origin. Ithanel rescued her at fifteen. She has been at the princess's side for eight years and the court has never once had occasion to name her.

nodes.name: Mistra
nodes.brief: Mistra is sixty-five and the Proprietress of La Casa de las Máscaras, which she built from the inside out over four decades into the most discreet establishment in Valdecorona. She knows things about half the city.

nodes.name: Ponnler
nodes.brief: The current leader of The Foragers of Life and owner of the seat of the Wing of Welfare. ## Appearance and personality

nodes.name: Ravena
nodes.brief: Ravena Solanel is Archbishopess of Arvela and head of The Root — which is to say the head of The Sowing entire, since the Root and The Branch are one Church. She is forty-four. She was born to peasants and rose on nothing but competence, which is rarer in the Church than the Church likes to say. Her faith is iron and her governance is combative. She keeps her seat in Lucerna.

nodes.name: Renzo
nodes.brief: Renzo is twenty-seven and the fixer of The Byway in Umbrales, the local link who knows what moves through the low quarter of Valdecorona and who moves it. He is discreet, forgettable by design, ruthless, and ambitious.

nodes.name: Rukhien
nodes.brief: Rukhien held **The Thimble** of the Court of Silk, the seat that absorbs. He absorbed the worst thing his people ever did and it broke him.

nodes.name: Sela Roquenegra
nodes.brief: Sela Roquenegra is Lady of House Roquenegra, thirty-six, and married into the house from a notable family of the central Arvelian lowlands. She is now entirely of La Marca. She is the house's external face — diplomacy, court, and the positioning of its claim in the succession — and she is the sharper political mind of the two who lead it.

nodes.name: Seravael
nodes.brief: Seravael, called The Needle, founded The Byway and leads it. She is a pure-blood vampire and she has spent centuries building the most extensive transnational network on the continent — one that most of the world does not know exists.

nodes.name: Storm
nodes.brief: Storm is the pet cat of Talassia, the current Wing of Commerce. ## Appearance and personality

nodes.name: Talassia
nodes.brief: The current leader of the The Feathers of Trade and seat of the Wing of Commerce. One of the most influential Faalari there are, she has relations with very powerful people. ## Appearance and personality

nodes.name: Tavaë
nodes.brief: Its people know exactly who it is. That is the difference between it and every other fixed point in the city.

nodes.name: The Elf Sown
aliases: The Mother of the Long Years
nodes.brief: The Elf Sown was the first elf and the mother of Aksa. She was the only one of the seven who ever loved another of them.

nodes.name: The Eye
nodes.brief: The Eye is Seravael's lieutenant in Arvela and one of the seven who run The Byway. He runs its **entire intelligence apparatus** — that is what the name means, and it is a job description rather than a title of honour. He spends far more of his existence managing information and disinformation than infiltrating anything.

nodes.name: The Faalari Sown
nodes.brief: The Faalari Sown is the primordial God of the Faalari, she is the one that created the first clans. His death during the Divine War at the hands of Aksa shook the land, literally, since the corpse of the once giant bird-god is what now a days is known as Valari mountain, the home of the Faalari.

nodes.name: The Human Sown
nodes.brief: The Human Sown was the first human, one of the seven placed in the world at the Sowing, and the father of Aksa. He died at the close of the Divine War, on the spot that is now the cathedral of Lucerna.

nodes.name: The Oni Sown
nodes.brief: The Oni Sown was the first Oni and the twin of the Vampire Sown. He was a master mask-forger, and his residue lives in the craft tradition itself rather than in any object or person: see Mask-forging.

nodes.name: The Selmari Sown
nodes.brief: Selmari names are one root remembered differently every time, and this is the extreme case of the rule. **No pure-blood has the root.** What reaches them does not arrive as a word — it arrives the way everything else it sends arrives, as impulse and certainty without a source — so each of them surfaced with a shape of a name and believed it was the name. *Ammaëra. Ammaërin. Ammaëth. Ammaë.* Every one of them is sure, and no two of them are saying the same thing.

nodes.name: The Vampire Sown
nodes.brief: The Vampire Sown was the first vampire and the twin of the Oni Sown. Every vampire alive descends from her. None of them knows her name.

nodes.name: Umaë
nodes.brief: Umaë is a pure-blood Selmari who walks the waking world, which almost none of them can, and is looking for the hidden seat of the vampires.

nodes.name: Vaen
nodes.brief: Vaën is one of the most conscious Selmari alive — far enough along the accumulation that he can lift and move objects without being a pure-blood, which almost none of them can. Among a people where sentience *is* rank, that places him near the top.

nodes.name: Vareth
nodes.brief: Vareth is a prince of Arvela and one of two co-claimants to its throne, the twin brother of Ithanel and elder son of Argavel and Alénor — or the younger, depending on which midwife is believed. He is a soldier by training and by public reputation, well loved in La Marca, and the favoured candidate of House Roquenegra. He has not declared a claim, and neither has his sister; the war over the succession is real and entirely unspoken, because the king is not yet dead.

nodes.name: Vashkien
nodes.brief: Vashkien is **The Thimble** of the Court of Silk — the seat that absorbs, the most resilient of the seven. He is the son of Rukhien, who held the same seat before him and vacated it by breaking.

nodes.name: Vernio
nodes.brief: Vernio is sixty-eight and has sold fruit from the northwest corner of the Market Plaza in Mercalia for forty years. His fruit is the best in Valdecorona and includes varieties out of Yongxi and Kurogane that nobody else in the plaza has and nobody knows how he gets. He does not explain it.

nodes.name: Yurael
nodes.brief: Yurael, called **Whitebloom**, is the head of the Tsubaki lineage and the first Yotsubaki — not descended from the attempt the two Sown made, but the attempt itself. She has been alive since then.

aToB.label: they have crossed paths
aToB.note: they have crossed paths. Eirvel recognised the magic and said nothing.

bToA.note: she is looking for him and does not know it is him.

secret.note: What she wants from the wandering healer is the Thirst. What she would find is something else: a being who gave up everything he loved for a duty nobody asked him to take, and who carries the weight of having killed his own family for a cause larger than any of them. The one person alive whose burden is shaped like hers. She would recognise that in about ten minutes of honest conversation. Neither of them has ten honest minutes to spare.

bToA.label: killed by
bToA.note: killed him with The White Jian at the close of the Divine War, extracted his power and sealed it. Aksa carries the swordsmanship of a man who beat him in single combat and the memory of a duel the oni still sing about without knowing whose.

bToA.label: killed and sealed by
bToA.note: killed it and sealed its power in a vessel, exactly as he sealed the other four, and does not know this one has a door his seal does not close. It has been reaching past him for generations.

bToA.label: see above
bToA.note: see above.

aToB.note: has noticed a resemblance between Aksa and Miren, and has told neither of them.
they knew each other before the war and they know each other now. He knows exactly what she is; she knows exactly what he is. She was made by two of the seven, and he killed both of them.

bToA.label: None
bToA.note: they knew each other before the war and know each other now. He killed both of her makers. Undecided in every other direction.

aToB.note: her teacher for ten years and the reason she is what she is. She has not seen him in a long time and does not know what became of him: he keeps a fruit stall in a Valdecorona market square now, and has told nobody in Arvela any of this.

bToA.note: his student, for ten years, back when he was a merchant of continental reputation. He taught her geography, trade, and the etiquette of dealing with each of the peoples, and she carried all of it home and taught it to her own.

aToB.label: brother, mutual contempt
aToB.note: his younger brother, the bishop who holds the Inquisition, and the contempt is mutual and total. Not about doctrine: Aldric is a soldier and Baldric ran.

bToA.label: elder brother, mutual contempt
bToA.note: his elder brother, and the contempt is mutual and total. Aldric cannot stand to look at him, and it is not about doctrine: Aldric is a soldier and Baldric ran. Baldric envies him for exactly the same fact.

aToB.label: his man
aToB.note: his man.

bToA.note: his lord, and the loyalty is a real accounting rather than a survival strategy: Aldric gave his people a life, a wage and a wall to stand behind, in a world that offers people like them very little. **Aldric did not have to make the arrangement work as well as it works.** Bras has served enough lords to know the difference, and he does not forget it.

aToB.label: the oni who struck Vareth without declaring
aToB.note: the oni who struck Vareth without declaring. He called a meeting over it and argued the oni's own code back at them; they stripped and exiled the man themselves. He demanded the duel in front of everyone and was told there was nobody left to challenge. See The parley on the Marca.

bToA.label: never met
bToA.note: never met. Aldric knows *someone* organises his mages and has deliberately chosen not to ask who; Eirvel considers that ideal, and the ignorance is maintained on purpose from both ends.

bToA.label: a rival, and the base of her brother's support
bToA.note: a rival, and the base of her brother's support.

aToB.note: his wife, and the sharper political mind of the two. He knows it and it does not trouble him.

bToA.label: her husband and her co-ruler
bToA.note: her husband and her co-ruler.

aToB.label: fought beside him
aToB.note: fought beside him. The loyalty is personal before it is political.

bToA.note: his strongest supporter, and a comrade from the border. La Marca bleeds for Vareth largely through Aldric.

aToB.label: see his article for the marriage
aToB.note: see his article for the marriage. They married for love, which the court found scandalous at the time — his class did not marry poor lesser-house girls — and has since forgotten. The forgetting does not suit her and she has never corrected it. Politics came afterwards.

bToA.note: they married for love, a fact the court found scandalous at the time and has since forgotten, which suits him. Politics came afterwards: he learned she was the finer political mind by the third month and made room for it. Twenty-three years of marriage, two children born in one night in the first year of it, and no other children ever — a singularity the court has spent twenty-three years quietly doing arithmetic on, and which he has refused for twenty-three years to explain to anyone.

secret.note: They tried once to speak about what comes after him. Neither has proposed the conversation again. Everything else between them is transparent — they hide the same kinds of things from each other for the same kinds of reasons and both know it. The one current asymmetry is the illness: she is entertaining hypotheses she has not voiced, he intuits that she is, and neither has spoken of it. That silence is the marriage's only wound, and both consider it survivable because they consider each other survivable, which is the deepest thing either has ever said about the other and neither has ever said aloud.

bToA.note: has begun entertaining hypotheses about the illness. None of them is yet him.

aToB.label: she reads her daughter completely
aToB.note: she reads her daughter completely: the machinery, the ambition, the arithmetic. She loves her precisely because she can see all of it.

bToA.note: her mother, and the one who taught her the work in the private margins of a tea hour. Ithanel now teaches Miren the same way.

aToB.label: filed as competent, discreet, unremarkable
aToB.note: filed as competent, discreet, unremarkable. The ordinary blindness of a mistress toward a servant, and one of the very few blindnesses in Alénor's life she has not caught in herself.

bToA.note: reads her accurately, and is read accurately in return.

aToB.note: she is among the very few who see through him, and she is also the one least able to act on it.

bToA.note: his patient of eleven years, who has never had cause to suspect him and has never ordered a search of his own chambers.

aToB.note: read with the wary respect a monarch reserves for a competent subordinate.

bToA.note: her father, who reads her as ambitious and administratively excellent in equal measure and has decided the combination is not a disqualification.

aToB.note: registered as competent household staff of unremarkable origin. He has never had cause to look twice and would not know how if he tried.

bToA.label: ideological ally, political rival
bToA.note: ideological ally, political rival. She upholds his legitimacy and disputes his powers in the same breath.

aToB.note: he reads his son as a father reads a boy who reminds him of his own younger self, which is precisely what Vareth has spent years arranging to be true without once articulating it. The father-lens is the only lens Vareth has never had to work to control.

bToA.label: he knows the king personally
bToA.note: he knows the king personally. Argavel stops at the stall when he can, and they get on. Years ago Vernio spoke before the king on behalf of the common people about something that needed changing, and the king listened, and the changes came.

aToB.label: uneasy ally
aToB.note: uneasy allies, and the alliance is real. Two bishops holding the two halves of the Church's hard power: Santaella has the missions, Baldric has the Inquisition. Together they are the counterweight to Ravena.

secret.note: He can tell the fanaticism is an act. He keeps Baldric anyway, because a convincing inquisitor pointed at the Root is worth a great deal — and because Baldric does the work properly. He despises him regardless, and **is not always able to keep it off his face.** Baldric has noticed. He wants Santaella's position, and Santaella wants more power than he currently has, and both of them know both halves.

bToA.label: an uneasy ally and a real one
bToA.note: an uneasy ally and a real one. Santaella has the missions, Baldric has the Inquisition: together, the counterweight to Ravena.

secret.note: The practitioner he has spent years failing to find is Des Terrao — and he is findable only because Baldric's desertion is what left him alive and with a reason to come back. Santaella will make contact without knowing any of it, and will be the one who brings him over the border. [!secret]- Known to: Santaella He can tell the fanaticism is performed, and keeps him anyway because the man does the work properly. He despises him for it and **cannot always keep that off his face.** Baldric has noticed, and wants his position.

aToB.label: subordinate she cannot remove
aToB.note: she cannot work out how a rat like this got as far as the Inquisition, and he costs her something almost daily. **He is not afraid to spill innocent blood**, and she cannot remove him.

bToA.note: the bishop holding the Inquisition, and she cannot work out how a man like that got that far. He costs her something almost daily and **he is not afraid to spill innocent blood.** She cannot remove him.

secret.note: **The debt she will not name.** Argavel backed her elevation seven years ago against three older and far better connected candidates. She considers that recognition of merit rather than favour, and if asked directly whether she owes him anything she would say no. She would believe it.

aToB.label: forced counterpart
aToB.note: she knows. Aldric keeps nothing from her and never has. And because she handles the house's politics, **she is the one who has to sit across from Baldric in person**, repeatedly, and be civil.

bToA.note: she knows what he did, because Aldric keeps nothing from her. And because she handles the house's politics, she is the one who has to sit across from him and be civil.

aToB.label: left him to die
aToB.note: the man he left to die.

secret.note: **Vareth lets it show on purpose.** Rage and disgust, plainly, on a face that has not shown anything real in years — a calculated risk taken because he could not hide it reliably anyway, and because being visibly human about something is worth more to him than the concealment was. Two reasons under it, and the second will not heal: Baldric gave him the scar, and Baldric cost him what Aldric has — the untouched war record, the legend without a mark on him. Vareth was going to be that. **Vareth has never said why**, out of respect for Aldric and the house. [!craft] It is the only real feeling Vareth shows anyone, and he shows it deliberately. Watching it does not catch him out — it teaches an observer something true while he is the one choosing that they see it.

aToB.label: his niece
aToB.note: his niece.

aToB.label: see the unresolved above
aToB.note: see the unresolved above.

aToB.label: the man he believes killed her
aToB.note: the man he believes killed her. Fifteen years of surveillance and public accusation, met with escorts.

bToA.note: his late wife's elder brother, who believes Santaella murdered her and has followed him for fifteen years. He is wrong, and Santaella treats him as what he appears to be: a broken veteran with a grievance, removed by escort whenever he gets close.

aToB.label: his younger sister
aToB.note: his younger sister. He loved her, lost her to a marriage he was not there for, and never spoke to her again.

bToA.label: her elder brother
bToA.note: her elder brother. He came home from the border to find her married and never heard from her again; he now believes her husband killed her, and has spent fifteen years saying so in public.

aToB.label: does not know he exists
aToB.note: does not know he exists.

bToA.note: a one-armed disinherited noble who has been tailing Lord Santaella through the city for years. Renzo is following him, and does not know why the man does it — only that he has never stopped.

aToB.label: aware of him
aToB.note: aware of him; no real bond.

aToB.label: his master, and the man who found him
aToB.note: his master, and the man who found him.

bToA.note: his first student, and his only channel into a great house.

aToB.label: a client at La Casa de las Máscaras
aToB.note: a client at La Casa de las Máscaras.

secret.note: She does not know he is a mage. She has connected the timing of his visits to Aldric Roquenegra's appearances in the city, and noted that he carries significantly more resources than his bearing accounts for — a man who moves like a soldier and spends like something else. Filed. She has not acted on it.

bToA.label: they have never met
bToA.note: they have never met.

secret.note: He carries the identical gift. He is the leader of the mages House Roquenegra shelters, and she is the woman hunting them. Same fire, opposite sides of the same hunt, and neither knows the other exists.

aToB.note: she trusts him exactly as far as Aldric does and treats him as a counterpart rather than a subordinate tolerated through her husband. He deals with both of them directly and has never needed to route through one to reach the other.

bToA.note: carries the mask that killed it, and does not know that it did, or that the city he walks into is the thing it killed. It cannot reach him; Aksa is inaccessible and a mask-wearer is standing on its own ground.

aToB.note: a friend he sees every night in what he believes is a recurring dream of his own. The city changes each time, Vaen does not, and the conversation picks up roughly where it left off. Bras has never questioned it beyond calling it *his save*.

secret.note: Because he believes he is inside his own head, Bras talks to Vaen without any of the discipline he applies to every waking hour. Vaen therefore knows everything: that he hates the name El Gato Negro, how much he worries about each of the March Mages, the whole shape of La Vela and Eirvel and the mask. Vaen knows more about him than Aldric Roquenegra does, and would never repeat a word of it.

bToA.note: his friend, who believes Vaën is a figure in a recurring dream of his own.

aToB.label: distant respect at a distance
aToB.note: distant respect at a distance. Aldric's man.
she admires the princess's intelligence from a distance and sees in her what she might have been under other circumstances. She has never said this to anyone and never will.

bToA.note: Santaella's daughter, seen at court, and nothing more than that yet.

secret.note: Cira admires her intelligence from a distance and sees in her what she might have been under other circumstances. She has never said this to anyone.

aToB.label: her father
aToB.note: her father. He does not know her.

bToA.label: his daughter and heir, whom he does not know
bToA.note: his daughter and heir, whom he does not know.
her daughter, whom she loved and beat, in that order and without ever seeing a contradiction.

aToB.note: he saw her at La Casa de las Máscaras without recognising her, and remembers her only as the woman with red hair.

secret.note: She has noticed something about Vareth that she cannot name. [!secret]- Known to: Cira and Vareth, neither aware of the other's half They had an encounter at the establishment. He was there for information; she was there for her own reasons and **recognised him**. She approached him masked. He took her for a very skilled professional and has no idea who she was.

aToB.note: the friendship is real on both sides, which is the remarkable part. Corian's loyalty has no known limit.

secret.note: He knows Vareth performs, and he stayed. He does not know about the cousin. It is not something he hides. It is something he has never put into words. Asked directly, he would say Vareth is a good man — and he would not be lying. He would be using the word differently than the asker.

bToA.note: a minor noble of La Marca and Vareth's only genuine attachment. The friendship is not a performance.

secret.note: Corián, who believes their friendship is what it looks like, is **the piece Vareth has stopped fully cataloguing.** He notices this about himself. He has not decided whether the noticing is a vulnerability, a resource, or the thing his catalogue was always missing — and suspects, on the mornings he permits himself the thought, that it is all three.

bToA.label: homura, and his to answer for
bToA.note: Homura, and his to answer for. The Marked struck without declaring, in front of his own, and lost. See The parley on the Marca.

aToB.label: rival across the two blood seats
aToB.note: the Kurayami Lord and his opposite number. Not brothers, but both pure-blood of the two seated lineages, so related somewhere back. The three centuries of protocol war between the seats is the two of them arguing about what honour is, in writing.

bToA.label: rival across the two blood seats
bToA.note: the Homura Lord. Not brothers, but both pure-blood of the two seated lineages, so related somewhere back. He needles him with the necklace; the Homura answers that there is no honour in those deaths, and means it.

aToB.note: they met as adults over an archive, and she believes he is a travelling elven scholar who enjoys testing her. They could fairly be called friends. He keeps what she tells him and has never moved it anywhere, which is character rather than policy. He also prefers her in the succession, on the single metric La Vela has: she is the less dogmatic of the twins about the Inquisition. He has no way to act on that preference and would not act on it if he had one.

secret.note: He can see that Ithanel carries the potential for Solar magic — the pure royal line — and has never told her.

bToA.note: one of the very few people she trusts with things she does not tell Miren. She believes he is a travelling elven scholar who enjoys testing her, and they met over an archive as adults. He keeps what she tells him and has never moved it either.

secret.note: He can tell she carries the potential for Solar magic — the pure royal line — and has never told her. He reads this from the **aura**, which is how he finds innate mages at all. There is nothing to see on her: her eyes are the ordinary jade of her father's line and will stay that way unless the gift ever wakes. He also quietly prefers her in the succession, on the only metric La Vela has: she is the less dogmatic of the twins about the Inquisition. He has no way to act on that and would not if he had.

aToB.label: see above
aToB.note: see above. He has never approached her.
a relationship of real trust, which is unusual for both.

bToA.note: friendship, which neither has ever admitted and both joke about. Eirvel is old enough that he knew immediately the man was hiding something, and he knows Seravael too — two pure-bloods of enormously long-lived peoples. He is a considerable ally of the network.

secret.note: The Eye does not know Miren exists. If he did, he would seek her out and bring her to Seravael. Vernio knows what Miren is and has said nothing, because he does not work for them.

aToB.label: old friendship
aToB.note: they were friends, before. She is one of the few left who knew him as a person rather than as a story, and that makes her the only member of the Court with a stake in Vashkien's private goal that is not Vashkien's own.

bToA.label: old friendship
bToA.note: they were friends, before.

aToB.label: sworn loyalty
aToB.note: her liege.

secret.note: Twenty-seven years ago she carried a newborn to Valdecorona and left her at the door of a noble house. Her orders were to place the child and then learn nothing further — deliberately, so that Seravael could never trace her through the person who had done it. She followed the order exactly. She does not know the house refused the child, that the girl grew up on the streets of Umbrales, or that she is alive today inside the palace. She does not know whose daughter she carried. [!craft] A perfectly executed instruction that produced the worst available outcome, and the execution is precisely why nobody ever found out. Nothing here should be narrated as her failure.

bToA.note: her favourite, and the only person she tells the truth to.

secret.note: Whatever Seravael actually feels, Ilvaen is where it goes. Not reports — the rest. It is the single crack in a life built on letting nobody in, and it has held for a very long time. Which is also why she chose her for the handover. Ilvaen is the finest and most invisible of the seven, she carries a Sown-forged mask, and she will execute an instruction to the letter including the part that says *learn nothing afterwards*. Seravael needed the one person capable of doing it perfectly and of never mentioning it again. She had exactly one.

aToB.label: she thinks well of him
aToB.note: she thinks well of him. He has more contact with the outside than anyone else in the Court and his informant network is well run; she respects competence and says so rarely.

bToA.note: The Strand, and in his professional judgement the finest spy in the network he runs. She can infiltrate anywhere and she is effective, and effectiveness is the thing he respects. The regard is entirely professional and entirely genuine.

aToB.note: she pities him for what he inherited, which he would hate to know.
a cautious ally and her natural constituency, courted patiently.

aToB.label: publicly her personal maid
aToB.note: publicly her personal maid. In fact her only real confidant, the only other person who knows what she saw, and the person she pulled out of a Valdecorona alley at seventeen. She has been teaching her ever since — reading, writing, three languages — in the same tea-hour margins where her own mother taught her. There is nothing operational she holds back from her.

bToA.note: the only relationship in her life, and absolute. It is not gratitude and it is not devotion and it is not the ordinary love a saved person has for a saviour, though it is not entirely none of those. She is the princess's sole confidant and the only other person who knows what Ithanel saw in her brother.

aToB.note: her pastoral anchor and her confessor, and the relationship is genuine on both sides rather than political.

secret.note: The Archbishopess told her about the gift herself, in confession, in her own words. It is the only time Ravena has said it aloud to anyone. Neither has referred to it since, in years, and Ithanel has never moved it anywhere. What Ithanel respects in her is that the faith is the genuine article — which is precisely what Ithanel does not have and knows she does not have. [!craft] She is also, without either of them using the word, the closest thing to a friend Ravena has: the only person in the Archbishopess's life who has never asked her for anything. Ravena is still waiting for the ask.

bToA.note: the princess who heard her confession, and the closest thing she has to company. See above.

aToB.note: opposite camps, and intellectual peers who can talk without pretence. The sharper of the Roquenegra pair, watched as carefully as she watches back. Both know how odd the arrangement is and neither has spoiled it.

bToA.label: unusual for two people in opposite camps
bToA.note: unusual for two people in opposite camps: intellectual peers who can talk honestly without pretense, and Sela has at points been something like a reference for the princess. Both are aware of how odd it is and neither has spoiled it.

aToB.note: her twin, her rival, and the person she is trying not to burn.

bToA.label: his twin and his rival
bToA.note: his twin and his rival. He performs affection for her that he no longer feels; she is among the few who see it.

aToB.note: the fruit-seller in the plaza, known by sight from the Alcázar and by reputation through Miren, who buys from him daily.
from a minor house, married for love rather than alliance, and the only person who ever agreed with him completely. She died of a long illness when Cira was small. See her article for who she was.

secret.note: He kept her body. What burned at the funeral was the maid who had nursed her through the last years — killed for the purpose and passed off as having left service in grief. He blames her for the death and considered the substitution **fitting**. See Residencia Santaella. He has spent the fifteen years since looking for a way to raise his wife, and has recently worked out what he needs.

bToA.note: married for love, and for the faith they shared. He has not accepted her death and does not intend to.

aToB.label: he does not read her as an enemy
aToB.note: he does not read her as an enemy. He reads her as someone whose thinking is too small for what the moment requires. She, for her part, names him as the first threat she would stop.

bToA.note: the threat she names first, and the measure of him is exact: she knows that if it were up to him she would be dead or out of the Church and he would be giving the orders. She reads him as a **fanatic and an irresponsible**, a man who cannot see one step past the burning.

secret.note: **She suspects him of his greatest crime and has nothing at all.** Not a document, not a witness, not a thread to pull. So in every room they share he remains what the evidence supports — a dangerous fanatic and a political adversary, not a criminal — and she has had to keep treating him as the second thing while believing the first. [!unresolved] What exactly she suspects She does not have the truth. What form her suspicion takes — that the rite was falsified, that the Yongxi missions are not what they claim, that something in that house is wrong — is undecided, and how close she is to the real answer decides how fast the whole thing can move. Note the symmetry before deciding: **she is hiding a gift her doctrine would burn her for, and so is he.** They are the two most powerful people in the Arvelan Church, each concealing a personal violation of the thing they enforce, each certain the other is the danger.

aToB.note: recruited her, used her because she was skilled and disposable in equal measure, and abandoned her. She does not know he is alive and operating a few streets from where he left her.

bToA.label: see above
bToA.note: see above. He would not recognise the name if he heard it.

aToB.label: her mother
aToB.note: her mother. Neither knows.

bToA.label: see above
bToA.note: see above. Her daughter, unknown to both of them.

aToB.label: visits, always at night
aToB.note: visits, always at night.

aToB.label: a client who uses the house as a working venue
aToB.note: a client who uses the house as a working venue. She has noticed the pattern of his visits and he correctly assumes she has.

secret.note: She has never identified him. Vareth does not know that.

bToA.note: Proprietress of La Casa de las Máscaras, which Vareth uses as a working venue. He assumes she has noticed the pattern of his visits and he is correct; he does not know that she has never identified him.

aToB.note: a devout and promising prince, in her reading, and the reading is wrong.

secret.note: He is cultivating her for the institutional weight of The Root and she has not noticed. Her blind spot is precise and almost poetic: she has spent her whole life judging the purity of other people's faith, and she cannot see a man performing devotion directly in front of her. Faith looks legible to her. It is the one thing she believes she can always read. [!craft] **She agrees with him. That is the problem.** Vareth advances a hard doctrinal line and does not believe a word of it. He holds no doctrinal position at all; he says it because it is what he has calculated she wants to hear, and he is right — it is her own position, argued for years, in public, on the record. He is not persuading her of anything. He is agreeing with her out loud and letting the agreement do the work. What he cannot see is that she is no longer in one piece behind it. She holds the position and carries the thing the position condemns, and every year of holding both has made the room between them narrower. So when he says what she has always said, she assents — and something in her goes quiet that never used to. **He watches her, and he has seen the right things.** Over a handful of council occasions he has clocked moments when her attention caught on something in the room nobody else registered — a servant passing, a small anomaly of temperature, once a candle that guttered against its own draft. He has filed the observations and connected them to nothing, because his catalog contains no category for divine magic; he assumes she is either eccentric or watching for something political he has not yet identified. Ravena knows he watches her, and **has decided the misidentification is currently useful.** She does not correct it. He reads the assent as success. The yield keeps coming in smaller than the effort and he will not understand why, because the obstacle is not disagreement. It is a woman agreeing with a doctrine she can no longer stand under. So the scene is two people performing a conviction neither of them still holds — he because he never held it, she because she cannot afford to admit she has stopped — and both of them believing the other means it.

aToB.label: his superior in the network
aToB.note: his superior in the network. He has barely seen him in person, respects him, and wants his position.

aToB.label: former liege
aToB.note: his former liege.

bToA.label: a friend, and what he became hurts her
bToA.note: a friend, and what he became hurts her.

secret.note: They disagreed about a great deal. It never touched the loyalty: whatever the argument, he never once wavered on the cause, and what he finally absorbed he absorbed for the whole species. She admires him for it and always did. She has not had him killed. She is not going to. [!unresolved] The internal politics of the Court Rukhien and Vashkien did not agree on everything and Vashkien holds his father's line on most of it. The actual fault lines inside the Court of Silk are undecided and worth deciding — they are the only politics the vampires have.

aToB.label: absorbed his error
aToB.note: the man whose error he absorbed.

bToA.label: see The Byway
bToA.note: see The Byway. The city that has no name was Aureval's mistake.

bToA.label: lost friend
bToA.note: a friend who stopped coming, long ago. Vaën does not know what happened to him.

aToB.label: father of
aToB.note: his son, who holds his seat and intends to free him or end him.

bToA.label: his father
bToA.note: his father.

aToB.note: she supports his claim without reservation, because he has given her no reason to doubt. He is the most plausible route to the Arvela she and Aldric want. Her evaluation of him is positive.

bToA.note: Aldric's wife and the external face of the house. Vareth respects her judgement more than her husband's and regards her as the real substance of the alliance.

aToB.label: her lieutenant in Arvela
aToB.note: her lieutenant in Arvela. Absolute trust, and it was not always there.

secret.note: When she learned what Aureval had done to the city with no name she was **furious** — more than at anything else in centuries. An enormous number of people died, and she has never once called it a solution. She calls it the error, because that is what it was. She kept him anyway. Not out of calculation: a leader who cannot forgive has nobody left after a century, and she could see what the thing had done to him. He has not made a second mistake since and he never will. **The worst error in the Court's history is the reason its intelligence apparatus is the best in the world**, and both of them know it, and neither has ever said it out loud. [!craft] She is capable of cold decisions. She is not a cold person, and the difference is the whole character. Do not write her weighing Aureval's error as an acceptable cost. She was angry, she stayed angry, and she forgave him anyway.

bToA.label: his liege
bToA.note: his liege. Absolute trust in both directions, and decades of service before that.

aToB.note: her ancestor, in the loose sense the word has among pure-bloods: descended from her, not a direct grandchild, and separated by an age. She never met her. What she has is the inheritance and the instruction — she knows why her Sown let herself be killed, and the first line of her own psyche comes straight from it.

bToA.label: descends from her
bToA.note: descends from her.

aToB.label: the Thimble, and he earned it
aToB.note: the Thimble, and he earned it.

secret.note: He was simply the best candidate, descent notwithstanding, and she gave him the seat on merit. He has never entirely believed her. What he suspects is that the table pities him — the son handed his father's emptied chair — and no amount of her saying otherwise reaches it, because she would say otherwise either way. She trusts him exactly as much as she trusts the rest, which is completely. And she hopes, without any evidence that it is possible, that a cure for Rukhien turns up in his lifetime.

bToA.label: sworn loyalty
bToA.note: his liege.

aToB.label: a friend, which is a short list
aToB.note: a friend, which is a short list. Long before the fruit stall he was a merchant of continental reputation, and he found the vampires **on his own**, without being told they existed, and traded with them. He has seen her face and has never mentioned it to anyone.

aToB.label: the pact, uncalled for centuries
aToB.note: the pact, uncalled for centuries.

secret.note: Yurael keeps vampires out of Kurogane; the Court owes her one unspecified favour in return, and she has never called it. Seravael is afraid of her, which is not a word that applies anywhere else in her life. Every other power on the board is bought, owed to, infiltrated or at minimum legible. Yurael is none of those: a wildcard running a great house in a nation the Court can barely operate in, holding a debt she can call on any morning she chooses. Seravael has spent centuries managing a threat that has never once moved against her.

bToA.label: None
bToA.note: the pact, uncalled for centuries, and the reason the Court of Silk does not expand into Kurogane.

aToB.note: The Thimble, and the son of the man who absorbed Aureval's worst error. They work together well and neither has ever let it damage the Court.

bToA.label: the man whose error his father absorbed
bToA.note: the man whose error his father absorbed. They work together well and the Court has never suffered for it. The resentment does not need an incident: it is renewed every time Aureval says Rukhien's name with respect.

aToB.label: twin
aToB.note: his twin. Blood magic descends from both of them at once.

bToA.label: her twin, and the one she stole from
bToA.note: her twin, and the one she stole from.

secret.note: She took the **Selmari mask** from her brother's forge and gave it to Aksa, who could not otherwise have reached the Selmari Sown at all. He returned it to her afterwards; she put it back so that her twin would never know it had gone. He found out regardless, before the duel that killed him. See The Selmari Sown.

aToB.note: the two of them made her, together and on purpose. She is the first and only thing the seven ever built jointly, she came out wrong, and she is still alive.

aToB.label: obstacle
aToB.note: a pure-blood who refused it and works against it. It is not concerned.

bToA.label: she hates it, comprehensively and personally
bToA.note: she hates it, comprehensively and personally.

aToB.note: hers and her twin's, made deliberately and imperfectly. The Yotsubaki carry her gene and her face; Yurael carries both awake, and is the only one who does.

aToB.label: frustrated friendship
aToB.note: a friend, and her longest disappointment.

secret.note: As a pure-blood she carries the **dawn tint** — rose into orange, running through the mist where a face would be. In the dream-state it is a pair of slowly turning irises; out here it is only the colour. See Selmari. It is also why nobody has ever described her twice the same way. The colour is exact while you are looking at it and gone from memory an hour later, so every account of her disagrees with every other account of her.

bToA.note: a friend, and the one who has come closest to moving him. She leads the small group opposed to the Sown's return and has asked him to join it more than once.
